from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Warm-up: Conditional Probability", [
            "Conditional probability defines likelihood given known info.",
            "P(A|B) is probability of A given B occurred.",
            "Sample space shrinks to region of B."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        formula = MathTex(r"P(A|B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        
        # Venn Diagram representation
        universe = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        event_b = Circle(radius=0.8, color="#FF0000", fill_opacity=0.3)
        event_a_overlap = Intersection(Circle(radius=1.0), Circle(radius=0.8).shift(LEFT*0.5), color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        # Positioning based on feedback (Line numbers from prompt instructions)
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B4', 'C6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_in_area(universe, 'B3', 'D5', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(event_b, 'C4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(event_a_overlap, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(formula), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"), run_time=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(universe), Create(event_b), run_time=2)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"), run_time=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(event_a_overlap), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(Indicate(formula), run_time=1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Events are independent if B gives no A info.",
            "Mathematically, P(A|B) equals P(A).",
            "Independent events do not influence each other."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining Independence", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Formula P(A∩B) = P(A) * P(B) + Asset dice.svg
        formula = MathTex(r"P(A \\cap B) = P(A) \\cdot P(B)", color=WHITE)
        dice_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/dice.svg")
        dice_icon.set_color(WHITE)
        
        content_1 = VGroup(formula, dice_icon).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(content_1, 'B4', 'B6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(formula), FadeIn(dice_icon))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Two separate boxes for events A and B
        box_a = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=1.5, color="#FFFF00")
        box_b = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=1.5, color="#FFFF00")
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=24, color=WHITE).next_to(box_a, UP, buff=0.1)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=24, color=WHITE).next_to(box_b, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        group_a = VGroup(box_a, label_a)
        group_b = VGroup(box_b, label_b)
        
        self.place_at_grid(group_a, 'C2', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(group_b, 'C5', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(group_a), FadeIn(group_b))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Intersection visualization + Asset marbles.svg
        intersection = Circle(radius=0.3, color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.5)
        marbles_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/marbles.svg")
        marbles_icon.set_color(WHITE)
        
        content_3 = VGroup(intersection, marbles_icon).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(content_3, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(content_3))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Bayes' Theorem reverses conditional probabilities.",
            "Formula connects P(A|B) and P(B|A).",
            "It updates prior beliefs with new evidence.",
            "Prior probability evolves into posterior probability.",
            "Used to diagnose rare events accurately."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Bayes' Theorem: The Logic of Reversal", lecture_lines)
        
        formula = MathTex(r"P(A|B) = \frac{P(B|A) \cdot P(A)}{P(B)}", color=WHITE)
        stethoscope = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/stethoscope.svg")
        prior_bar = Rectangle(height=0.5, width=2, color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.5)
        evidence_bar = Rectangle(height=0.5, width=2, color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.5)
        prior_label = Text("P(A)", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        evidence_label = Text("P(B)", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'A2', 'B5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(stethoscope, 'A6', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(Write(formula), FadeIn(stethoscope))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(prior_bar, 'D2', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(prior_label, 'D1', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(evidence_bar, 'D5', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(evidence_label, 'D6', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Create(prior_bar), Write(prior_label), Create(evidence_bar), Write(evidence_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Swap(prior_bar, evidence_bar))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Highlight P(B|A) in the formula. MathTex parts index carefully
        p_b_given_a = formula[0][2:7]
        self.play(Indicate(p_b_given_a, color="#FF00FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(stethoscope.animate.scale(2).move_to(self.grid['E4']))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Independence simplifies Bayes' Theorem calculations.",
            "Decision trees visualize Bayesian updating processes.",
            "AI filters apply this to identify spam."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis and Practical Application", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        mailbox_svg = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mailbox.svg", color=WHITE)
        
        # Elements
        problem_box = Rectangle(width=4, height=2, color=WHITE)
        problem_label = Text("Spam Detection Problem", font_size=20).move_to(problem_box.get_center())
        problem_group = VGroup(problem_box, problem_label, mailbox_svg)

        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color=GREEN) for _ in range(10)])
        dots.arrange_in_grid(2, 5, buff=0.2)
        
        result_label = Text("P(Spam | Keywords) High", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        result_mailbox = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mailbox.svg", color=YELLOW)
        result_group = VGroup(result_label, result_mailbox).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.place_in_area(problem_group, 'A2', 'B5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(problem_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(dots, 'D2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(dots))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(result_group, 'E2', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Write(result_group))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Bayes' Theorem and Independence: Unlocking Predictive Logic

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: Conditional Probability
sections.content: Briefly define conditional probability P(A|B) as 'the probability of A given that B has already occurred.' Use a Venn diagram animation to show the 'shrinking' sample space from the full area to just the region of B.
sections.example: Visualizing a bag of marbles: If you know the marble drawn is red (Event B), how does that change the probability it came from Box 1 (Event A)?

sections.title: Defining Independence
sections.content: Define independence as a state where knowing Event B gives no information about Event A. Mathematically: P(A|B) = P(A). Use a graphic showing two independent coins: one outcome does not move the needle on the other's probability.
sections.example: Flipping a coin (Event A) and rolling a die (Event B). The outcome of the coin does not change the probability distribution of the die.

sections.title: Bayes' Theorem: The Logic of Reversal
sections.content: Introduce Bayes' Theorem as a bridge between P(A|B) and P(B|A). Present the formula: P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B). Use an animated flow chart showing the 'Prior' probability being updated by 'Evidence' to reach a 'Posterior' probability.
sections.example: A 'Medical Diagnostic' scenario: A character (Dr. Owl) wants to know the probability a patient has a rare disease (A) given they tested positive (B), considering the test's accuracy (P(B|A)).

sections.title: Synthesis and Practical Application
sections.content: Summarize how independence simplifies Bayes' Theorem (if events are independent, the theorem collapses). Conclude with a visual 'Decision Tree' that demonstrates how Bayesian updating works in AI and machine learning systems.
sections.example: A spam filter bot: Using Bayes' Theorem to calculate the probability an email is 'Spam' (A) based on the presence of specific keywords (B), updating the filter's certainty over time.
